reviews.text: Days Since Habit Tracker App. I have thoroughly enjoyed using the days since app to track my habits that I wanted so badly to change and I have successfully reached 298 days. And the entire 298 days I have used this app to track it. I want to be honest with my review and so that means I have to state the issues with the app and honestly the only issue I have come across is that it’s so easy somehow to reset the counter through the widget. I have reset my counter several times on accident somehow. The first time I done it I was so disappointed and upset but then I learned how to take away the reset thankfully. I have worked so hard on my habit that when I first reset it I was truly devastated but now that I know how to fix the issue it’s been fine. I would just ask if there is a way to not have the reset function so easily accessible or able to be done on accident. If there was like a confirmation question or something that would be helpful because then it’s a lot less likely to accidentally hit the correct buttons more than once in a row. But other than the one issue I have ran into the app has been amazing. I do think at times that the app should somehow give motivational quotes or some type of support to the customer and not just have it only to track the time. It would be a lot more enticing to people if it offered some type of support or interaction.

You can literally get a day counter app and just reset it whenever you relapse for free. This is a horrible price for such a small feature. Maybe if it was around 2-5 dollars this would be a good price. The amount of developing it takes to create something like this is so small and lazy. All you need is a day counter which is easy to code, a widget design which is easy to add, and something to reset it. that’s it. Whoever programmed this app probably didn’t even need 17 dollars to create the small amount of code needed for this. It’s absurd and you shouldn’t support these greedy developers taking advantage of addicts.

reviews.text:
An end to addictions. Because of this app alone, I can say I have not been on Instagram/TikTok for 523 days, after previously spending hours and hours a day wasting my life to doomscrolling.

The reason this app works is that each counter is a commitment to yourself to a goal, and a personal challenge to hit a certain number of days. In seeing a tangible number (easily visible as a widget on your phone), it helps to remind you of your end goal. As that number grows, you become more and more empowered to keep going. 

I love this app for its simplicity and effectiveness in ending bad habits. I would recommend it to anyone.
